title: Overview of bycatch package
text: Previous authors, including Gardner et al. (2008) Martin et al. (2015) assumed rare even bycatch follows Poisson process, observed bycatch events yty_{t} modeled according estimated bycatch rate λ\lambda, p(yt|λ)=e−λλytyt!p(y_{t}|\lambda) = e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^{y_{t}}}{y_{t}!} λ\lambda mean Poisson distribution. mean rate parameter λ\lambda can decomposed per - event (e.g. set) parameter number observed sets ntn_{t}, λ=θ*nt\lambda = \theta * n_{t}. GLM setting, log-link function often used model effects covariates, e.g. log(λ)=log(θ)+b1*x1+b2*x2...log(\lambda) = log(\theta) + b_{1}*x_{1} + b_{2}*x_{2}..., setting known number sets ntn_{t} treated offset, log(λ)=log(θ)+b1*x1+b2*x2+log(nt)log(\lambda) = log(\theta) + b_{1}*x_{1} + b_{2}*x_{2} + log(n_{t}). Estimation λ\lambda θ\theta can done maximum likelihood Bayesian setting, use Bayesian methods estimate posterior distribution parameters given observed bycatch data, p(θ|𝐲_)∝p(θ)p(𝐲_|θ)p(\theta|\underline{\mathbf{y}}) \propto p(\theta)p(\underline{\mathbf{y}}|\theta)

Two additional extensions models zero-inflated extensions. adopt hurdle models model extra zeros, p(yt=0)=ϕp(y_{t}=0) = \phi p(yt>0)=1−ϕp(y_{t}>0) = 1-\phi. addition Poisson Negative Binomial models, adopt three continuous distributions: Gaussian (“normal”), Gamma (“gamma”) lognormal (“lognormal”). Log-link functions specified mean distribution. Gaussian model, estimate variance parameter, σ\sigma, given Student-t(3,0,2) prior distribution. Similarly, Gamma distribution, put Student-t(3,0,2) prior coefficient variation (CV), assumed constant across observations. Finally, lognormal distribution, estimate lognormal variance assume constant across observations.

title: Multi-stream monitoring
text: can verify multi-stream gives similar results pooling: Extract compare estimated rates: rates similar, confirming multi-stream mode properly pools information across streams.
code: # Manually pool the data d_pooled <- d d_pooled$Takes_pooled <- d$Takes_obs + d$Takes_em d_pooled$Sets_pooled <- d$Sets_obs + d$Sets_em  # Fit pooled model fit_pooled <- fit_bycatch(   Takes_pooled ~ 1,   data = d_pooled,   time = "Year",   effort = "Sets_pooled",   family = "poisson",   time_varying = FALSE ) # Multi-stream: lambda_base is rate per unit effort lambda_multi <- rstan::extract(fit$fitted_model, "lambda_base")$lambda_base rate_multi <- mean(lambda_multi)  # Single-stream: lambda is expected count, divide by effort lambda_pooled <- rstan::extract(fit_pooled$fitted_model, "lambda")$lambda rate_pooled <- mean(lambda_pooled[, 1]) / d_pooled$Sets_pooled[1]  cat("Multi-stream rate:", round(rate_multi, 4), "\n") ## Multi-stream rate: 0.0137 cat("Pooled rate:", round(rate_pooled, 4), "\n") ## Pooled rate: 0.0138

text: Coverage Rates vs effort_total: function supports two approaches calculating unobserved effort: Coverage rates (recommended): Use covrate, covrate_obs, covrate_em, covrate_both specify percentage fishery monitored. function calculates unobserved effort : observed_effort * ((100 - coverage) / coverage) Total effort: Use effort_total provide total fishery effort directly. Unobserved effort calculated : effort_total - observed_effort NOTE: effort_total must units effort columns Priority order: effort_total > coverage rates > 100% coverage assumed Multi-stream monitoring: using multiple monitoring streams (Observer, EM, ), data kept separate statistical model share underlying bycatch rate. approach assumes monitoring types perfect/equal detection (detection = 100%) avoids distributional issues arise pooling.
